newsitem.title: CHINA: Oilfield in northwest China eyes foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: Oilfield in northwest China eyes foreign funds.

text.p: Chinese authorities have decided to open part of an oilfield in northwest China to foreign investment, the China News Service said on Friday.

About 17,700 square kilometres of Changqing oilfield, located in the basin covering parts of Shaanxi, Gansu and Ningxia provinces, would be open to foreign investment through international tenders, it said without giving details.
Foreign investment would boost exploration and development of Changqing's oil and natural gas reserves, it said.
The oilfield is estimated to have reserves of 134 million tonnes of crude and 170 billion cubic metres of natural gas, the China News Service said. It gave no further details.
Changqing oilfield was expected to produce 2.6 million tonnes of crude in 1996, state media has said.
